original_question: Let (X, omega) be a compact n-dimensional Kahler manifold, and let phi in E(X, omega) solve (omega + dd^c phi)^n = f omega^n where f is L^1 and smooth away from a divisor D subset X. Determine whether phi is smooth on X minus D.
target_in_paper: Question 22 (DiNezza-Lu) in §3.4, "Smooth currents in big cohomology classes." It is the divisor-version regularity question stated immediately after the nearby big-class smoothness Question 21. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the official problem almost verbatim: a compact Kähler manifold, an unknown φ in E(X,ω), the equation (ω+dd^cφ)^n = fω^n, the assumption f ∈ L^1 and smooth away from a divisor D, and the question whether φ is smooth on X\D. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
missing_details: The paper means n = dim_C X, i.e. complex dimension n. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, E(X,ω) should be unpacked: by Definition 2.2 it is the finite-energy class of ω-plurisubharmonic functions whose normalized Monge-Ampère measure MA(φ) is a probability measure. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

Because the unknown lies in E(X,ω), the equation is understood in the finite-energy/non-pluripolar Monge-Ampère sense, not as a priori a classical pointwise equation. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

It is cleaner to state f as a density in L^1(X,ω^n) that is C^∞ on X\D. The paper's formal statement does not impose a sharper asymptotic model for f, even though the surrounding motivation mentions divisorial-type singularities f ≈ ||σ||^a. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

If one wants the question to be fully self-contained, one can mention the paper's nearby existence-uniqueness remark: since μ = fω^n is non-pluripolar, there exists a unique normalized solution φ ∈ E(X,ω); the issue is its regularity on X\D. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
refined_question: Let (X,ω) be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension n, let D ⊂ X be a divisor, and let φ ∈ E(X,ω) be an ω-plurisubharmonic finite-energy solution of the complex Monge-Ampère equation (ω + dd^cφ)^n = f ω^n on X, where f ∈ L^1(X,ω^n) and f is C^∞ on X\D. Must φ be C^∞ on X\D? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, since μ := fω^n is non-pluripolar, one may ask whether the unique normalized solution φ ∈ E(X,ω) of (ω + dd^cφ)^n = μ is smooth on X\D. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets the divisor regularity problem in §3.4 rather than any neighboring question: the combination of hypotheses "f ∈ L^1," "smooth off a divisor D," and the conclusion sought "smooth on X\D" appears precisely in Question 22. The only paper-faithful additions needed to make it fully stand-alone are to unpack E(X,ω) via Definition 2.2 and to clarify that the equation is interpreted in the finite-energy/non-pluripolar sense; the sentence immediately following Question 22 supplies the paper's own equivalent reformulation via the unique normalized solution. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
